title: Istanbulkart Mastery: The only ticket that matters
excerpt: İstanbul’s all-in-one transport card: one tap covers the metro, tram, bus, ferries, Marmaray, Metrobüs, funiculars, and more. Buy it once (₺165 for the anonymous card), load travel credit, and it’s the cheapest, simplest way to get around the city.
bodyHtml:
Where to Buy an İstanbulkart

You can purchase an İstanbulkart from:

  • Yellow Biletmatik ticket machines

  • Newsstands

  • Kiosks near major metro, tram, and ferry stations

An anonymous İstanbulkart costs ₺165 (card only, no credit on it); a personalised card registered in your name is ₺140. After buying your card, load travel credit and you’re ready to go. Prices change — the official İstanbulkart price list linked below has the current ones.

Most Biletmatik machines accept cash, while many also accept Turkish bank cards.

Arriving at the Airport

İstanbul Airport (IST)

The cheapest way to reach the city is:

M11 Metro → Gayrettepe → M2 Metro

Purchase your İstanbulkart from the yellow ticket machines near the metro entrance before starting your journey.

The M11 Airport Metro uses distance-based pricing. A maximum fare is temporarily charged when you enter. After tapping out at your destination, the correct fare is calculated automatically, and any unused balance is automatically refunded to your card.

Sabiha Gökçen Airport (SAW)

Take the M4 Metro into the city and connect to Istanbul’s wider public transport network.

If you plan to use airport coaches such as Havaist or Havabus, keep a bank card or some cash available. Our airport guide covers every route into the city.

Register Your Card

Registering your İstanbulkart provides several benefits:

  • Protects your balance if your card is lost or stolen.

  • Makes online top-ups easier.

  • Gives access to certain discounts and special programs.

You can register your card through the official İstanbulkart app or website.

Transfer Discounts

One of the biggest advantages of using an İstanbulkart is discounted transfers: up to five transfers within two hours of your first tap, subject to the applicable fare rules.

Each additional transfer costs less than the previous one, making journeys involving multiple connections significantly cheaper than paying separate full fares.

Typical Public Transport Fares (from 20 July 2026)

  • 🚇 Metro, Tram & Bus: ₺46.20 full fare with an İstanbulkart

  • 🎫 Single-Use Ticket (BİRgeç): ₺65

  • 🚆 Marmaray: Distance-based

  • 🚍 Metrobüs: Distance-based

  • ✈️ M11 Airport Metro (IST): Distance-based

  • ⛴️ City Ferries: Varies by line and operator

  • 🏝️ Princes’ Islands Ferries: Distance-based (varies by operator and destination)

Distance-based services such as Marmaray, Metrobüs and the M11 Airport Metro vary depending on how far you travel. Istanbul's fares rise at least once a year, so treat these as a guide.

Can I Use My Bank Card Instead?

Yes.

Contactless payment is accepted at many validators across the network with:

  • Credit cards

  • Debit cards

  • Mobile wallets (where supported)

However:

  • Don't expect İstanbulkart transfer discounts.

  • You may pay more than İstanbulkart users — check the fare shown when you tap.

  • Not every service accepts it yet, so don't rely on it as your only way to pay.

Using a bank card is convenient as a backup, but an İstanbulkart offers the best value for most visitors.

Discounts Available

Students

Eligible students get discounted fares (₺22.55 a ride from 20 July 2026) and a discounted monthly subscription (₺653). Eligibility — including for international students — is set by İstanbul Metropolitan Municipality, so check before you apply.

Seniors

Eligible residents receive reduced fares and discounted monthly subscriptions.

Children Under 6

Children under six travel free when accompanied by an adult.

The Mavi (Blue) Card

If you live in Istanbul and use public transport frequently, the Mavi Kart may save you money.

  • A monthly subscription with a fixed ride allowance — check the current limit when you buy it

  • ₺3,628 per month (from 20 July 2026)

  • Best suited for regular commuters

Don’t Skip the Ferries

Ferries are no longer the cheapest way to cross Istanbul, but they remain one of the city’s most enjoyable experiences.

Enjoy:

  • Beautiful Bosphorus views

  • Fresh sea air

  • A more relaxing journey than crowded metro lines

For many locals, ferries are still the best way to travel between the European and Asian sides.

Common Mistakes

1. Running Out of Credit

Always keep some balance on your card before entering stations.

2. Buying Single-Use Tickets

At 65 TRY each, they quickly become more expensive than owning an İstanbulkart.

3. Forgetting to Tap Out

Distance-based services such as the M11 Airport Metro, Marmaray and Metrobüs charge a maximum fare when you tap in; tap out at your destination so the correct fare is calculated and the difference refunded.

4. Assuming Every Machine Accepts Cards

Some ticket machines still accept cash only, so it’s a good idea to carry a little cash.

5. Sharing One İstanbulkart

Each traveller should ideally have their own İstanbulkart to benefit from transfer discounts and enjoy a smoother journey.

Final Tip

If you’re new to Istanbul, the public transport system may seem overwhelming at first. Once you have an İstanbulkart, exploring the city becomes simple, affordable, and efficient.
